families.label: Whole tree
families.title: Gods and heroes
families.note: Every figure, from the first gods to the last of both houses.

families.label: The gods
families.title: The gods
families.note: From Gaia and Uranus to the younger gods.

notes.E: In Homer, Aphrodite is the daughter of Zeus and Dione, and Hera bears Typhon alone.
notes.H: In Hesiod, Aphrodite rises from the foam round Uranus’ severed flesh, and Hera bears Hephaestus alone.
notes.T: Lyric and tragedy tell 8 of the 149 links among the gods; in Aeschylus, Night is the mother of the Erinyes.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Aphrodite is a daughter of Zeus and Dione, and Metis’ drug makes Cronus bring up his children.
notes.L: Later writers tell 14 of the 149 links among the gods; in Pausanias, Nemesis is a daughter of Ocean.

families.label: The Titans
families.title: The Titans
families.note: Gaia and Uranus, their twelve children, and the gods the Titans fathered.

notes.E: In Homer, Uranus and Gaia fade: the family begins with Cronus and Rhea, and with Ocean and Tethys.
notes.H: In Hesiod, Dione is a daughter of Ocean and Tethys, and Zeus marries Metis and Themis as well as Hera.
notes.T: Lyric and tragedy tell 4 of the 119 links here; in Aeschylus, Themis is the mother of Prometheus.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Dione is a daughter of Uranus and Gaia, and Metis’ drug makes Cronus bring up his children.
notes.L: Later writers tell 9 of the 119 links here, among them Rhea’s stone and Pyrrha, daughter of Pandora.

families.label: Zeus and his loves
families.title: Zeus and his loves
families.note: His wives and lovers, and the children they bore him.

notes.E: In Homer, Zeus does not come to Leda as a swan, and in the Cypria Nemesis is Helen’s mother.
notes.H: In Hesiod, Zeus marries Metis first, then Themis; Leda, Danaë and Ganymede fade.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, Zeus comes to Leda as a swan and to Danaë as gold, but his marriage to Hera fades.
notes.A: Apollodorus tells 57 of the 64 links here; Metis and Themis are not called Zeus’ wives, nor Tantalus his son.
notes.L: In later writers, Nemesis flees Zeus through many shapes, and Asteria escapes him as a quail.

families.label: Thebes
families.title: Thebes, from Cadmus to Antigone
families.note: The house of Cadmus and the Labdacids.

notes.E: In Homer, Oedipus kills his father, weds his mother and curses his sons, but no children are named as theirs.
notes.H: Hesiod tells only Cadmus, Harmonia and their children; Laius and Oedipus fade.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, Jocasta bears Oedipus four children, and Creon condemns Antigone.
notes.A: Apollodorus tells 44 of the 46 links here, Laius and Chrysippus among them; only Pelops’ curse is missing.
notes.L: In later writers, Pelops curses Laius for carrying off Chrysippus; Oedipus’ curse on his sons fades.

families.label: Perseus and Heracles
families.title: Perseus and Heracles
families.note: The house of Perseus, from Danaë’s prison to Heracles on Olympus.

notes.E: In Homer, Eurystheus, son of Sthenelus, rules over Heracles, but most of the labours and both his wives fade.
notes.H: In Hesiod, the Nemean Lion is a son of Orthus and Ladon a child of Phorcys and Ceto; Megara and her sons fade.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, Heracles kills Megara and their sons, and wrestles Death for Alcestis.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Andromeda bears Perseus his sons, and Eurystheus’ mother is Nicippe, a daughter of Pelops.
notes.L: In Ovid, Athena turns Medusa’s hair to snakes, and Perseus turns Atlas into a mountain.

families.label: The Argonauts
families.title: Jason and the Argonauts
families.note: The house of Aeolus, the Golden Fleece, and Medea.

notes.E: In Homer, Jason appears only as Hypsipyle’s lover on Lemnos; Medea and all she does fade.
notes.H: In Hesiod, Jason marries Medea, daughter of Aeetes, but none of her killings is told.
notes.T: In Pindar, Jason himself kills the serpent that guards the fleece; Poseidon and Tyro fade.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Orpheus is a son of the Muse Calliope, and Poseidon blinds Phineus for showing the way.
notes.L: In later writers, Medea makes old Aeson young again, and the serpent that guards the fleece is Typhon’s.

families.label: Troy
families.title: The house of Priam
families.note: From Dardanus, son of Zeus, to the fall of Troy.

notes.E: In Homer, Menelaus fights Paris and Achilles kills Troilus; Polyxena and Cassandra’s curse fade.
notes.H: Hesiod tells Dardanus, Tithonus and Eos, and Aphrodite’s love for Anchises; Priam’s house fades.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, Neoptolemus sacrifices Polyxena and Helen marries Deiphobus; Troy’s older kings fade.
notes.A: Apollodorus tells 71 of the 74 links here; Hecuba is Troilus’ mother, and Menelaus kills Deiphobus.
notes.L: In later writers, Neoptolemus throws Astyanax from the walls and sacrifices Polyxena; Paris and Helen fade.

families.label: The children of Heracles
families.title: The children of Heracles
families.note: His wives and lovers, his sons and daughters, and their war with Eurystheus.

notes.E: In Homer, Heracles’ son Tlepolemus sails to Troy, but Deianira, Hyllus and Megara’s sons fade.
notes.H: In Hesiod, Hyllus is Heracles’ son by Deianira, but Megara and the revenge on Eurystheus fade.
notes.T: In Euripides, Iolaus, young again for a day, brings Eurystheus down; Hyllus does not kill him.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Hyllus kills Eurystheus, and Megara marries Iolaus instead of dying by Heracles’ hand.
notes.L: In later writers, Macaria is Heracles’ daughter by Deianira; the revenge on Eurystheus fades.

families.label: Theseus and Athens
families.title: Theseus and Athens
families.note: The kings of Athens, from the earth-born Erichthonius to Theseus, and the Cretan family he married into.

notes.E: In Homer, Pirithous is a son of Zeus and Theseus of Aegeus; the Minotaur and Phaedra fade.
notes.H: Hesiod tells 13 of the 67 links here; Theseus loves Ariadne, but his parents are not named.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, Poseidon is Theseus’ father too, and Theseus curses Hippolytus; the Minotaur fades.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Poseidon makes Pasiphae love the bull, and Hades holds Theseus and Pirithous fast.
notes.L: In later writers, Medea tries to poison Theseus and he kills the Minotaur; Poseidon’s curse on Pasiphae fades.

families.label: The Odyssey
families.title: The Odyssey
families.note: The house of Odysseus, the women who kept him and the enemies he made, on the way to Troy and the long way home.

notes.E: In Homer, Laertes is Odysseus’ only father, and Polyphemus’ curse keeps him from home; Telegonus fades.
notes.H: Hesiod tells 10 of the 56 links here, among them Circe and Calypso; Odysseus’ parents and wife fade.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, Sisyphus lies with Anticleia and may be Odysseus’ father; the wanderings fade.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Telegonus kills Odysseus and marries Penelope, and Scylla is a daughter of Phorcys.
notes.L: In later writers, Telemachus marries Circe, and Circe turns Scylla into a monster.

families.label: The Seven against Thebes
families.title: The Seven
families.note: Seven champions from Argos at the seven gates of Thebes, the families they came from, and the sons who finished their war.

notes.E: In Homer, Althaea curses her son Meleager, and Diomedes wounds Ares; Oedipus’ children fade.
notes.H: Hesiod tells 9 of the 54 links here, chiefly the house of Calydon; the Seven and Oedipus’ sons fade.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, Creon condemns Antigone, Haemon’s bride; Meleager’s parents fade.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Athena withholds immortality from Tydeus and blinds Tiresias; Diomedes does not wound Ares.
notes.L: In later writers, Alcmaeon kills his mother Eriphyle and Meleager loves Atalanta; Oedipus’ curse fades.

families.label: Bellerophon and Corinth
families.title: Bellerophon
families.note: From Sisyphus of Corinth to Bellerophon and the Chimera, and his grandsons, who fought for Troy.

notes.E: In Homer, Glaucus is Bellerophon’s father, and his daughter Laodamia bears Zeus a son, Sarpedon.
notes.H: In Hesiod, Poseidon is Bellerophon’s father and Pegasus is born of Medusa; the Lycian line fades.
notes.T: In Euripides, Bellerophon drops Stheneboea into the sea, and Pegasus throws him when he rides for Olympus.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Glaucus is Bellerophon’s father; Pegasus’ fall and Sarpedon’s birth fade.
notes.L: In later writers, Poseidon is Bellerophon’s father; his wife and children fade.

families.label: The house of Minos
families.title: The house of Minos
families.note: Europa’s sons in Crete, the children of Minos and Pasiphae, and Daedalus, who built for them and fled them.

notes.E: In Homer, Deucalion is Minos’ son and Idomeneus his grandson; Pasiphae and the Minotaur fade.
notes.H: In Hesiod, Zeus carries Europa to Crete and Minos is their son; Pasiphae and the Minotaur fade.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, Catreus gives his daughter Aerope away, and she marries Atreus; Minos’ parents fade.
notes.A: Apollodorus tells 56 of the 57 links here, with Catreus’ children, Palamedes’ parents and Medea against Talos.
notes.L: In later writers, Athena turns Perdix into a partridge, and Cocalus’ daughters scald Minos to death.

families.label: Io and the Danaids
families.title: Io and the Danaids
families.note: From the river Inachus and his daughter Io, whom Zeus loved, through Egypt and back to Argos with the fifty daughters of Danaus, down to Acrisius, Danaë and Andromeda.

notes.E: In Homer, Zeus comes to Danaë as gold; Io, Danaus and the Danaids fade.
notes.H: Hesiod tells 5 of the 58 links here; Zeus loves Io and swears to Hera he never touched her.
notes.T: In Aeschylus, Libya is Epaphus’ daughter and Belus her son, and the Danaids wed the sons of Aegyptus.
notes.A: Apollodorus tells all 58 links here; Poseidon fathers Belus and Agenor on Libya, and Nauplius on Amymone.
notes.L: In later writers, Hypermnestra marries Lynceus and their line runs down to Danaë; Libya and Belus fade.

families.label: Monsters and their killers
families.title: The monsters
families.note: The brood of the sea gods Phorcys and Ceto and of Typhon and Echidna, and the heroes who killed them: Perseus, Bellerophon, Heracles and Oedipus.

notes.E: Homer tells 9 of the 90 links here; Hera bears Typhon alone, and Echidna’s brood fades.
notes.H: In Hesiod, Echidna is a daughter of Phorcys and Ceto, and the Sphinx and the Nemean Lion are children of Orthus.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, the heroes kill the monsters, but who bore them fades.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Echidna is a daughter of Tartarus and Gaia, and Typhon fathers the Nemean Lion.
notes.L: In later writers, Typhon and Echidna also bear Scylla and the serpent that guards the fleece.

families.label: Orpheus and the underworld
families.title: The underworld
families.note: Night and her sons Sleep and Death, Hades and Persephone, those who went down and came back, and those who stay below for ever.

notes.E: In Homer, Pirithous is a son of Zeus; Orpheus’ parents and death fade.
notes.H: In Hesiod, Night marries Erebus and bears Hypnos and Thanatos; the punishments in Hades fade.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, Heracles wrestles Thanatos for Alcestis, and Artemis kills Tityos.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Orpheus is Calliope’s son, Apollo’s only in name, and Hades binds Theseus and Pirithous.
notes.L: In later writers, Ixion is Pirithous’ father, and the Maenads tear Orpheus to pieces.

families.label: The Trojan War
families.title: The Trojan War
families.note: From the apple of Eris to the fall of Troy and the wrecks on the way home: the quarrels of the Iliad, the allies who came to Priam, and the killings on the last night.

notes.E: In Homer, Achilles kills Eetion, Hector kills Patroclus, and Menelaus fights Paris; Cassandra’s curse fades.
notes.H: In Hesiod, Eris is a daughter of Night and Thetis marries Peleus; the fighting at Troy fades.
notes.T: In lyric and tragedy, Odysseus leaves Philoctetes on Lemnos, and Helen marries Deiphobus.
notes.A: In Apollodorus, Athena wrecks the ship of Ajax the Lesser and Menelaus kills Deiphobus; Patroclus’ death fades.
notes.L: In later writers, Neoptolemus kills Astyanax and Polyxena; Paris’ taking of Helen fades.
